variable_coverage.construction: The absolute value of discretionary accruals. Discretionary accruals equal total accruals minus nondiscretionary accruals; nondiscretionary accruals are estimated from the supporting OLS model.

At the six-digit input-output industry level, the focal industry’s supplier-industry R&D measure is the sum across supplier industries (excluding the focal industry) of each supplier industry’s annual R&D expense divided by total assets, weighted by its input coefficient: dollars of that supplier industry’s output used to produce one dollar of focal-industry output. Industry R&D is aggregate Compustat R&D expense divided by aggregate industry assets; missing R&D values are set to zero. Where a six-digit IO industry has no Compustat firms, the authors use firms at the five-, four-, two-, then one-digit level. IO weights use the 1987 Use table for 1984–1989, the 1992 table for 1990–1994, and annual updates of the 1992 benchmark tables for 1995–2003.

At the six-digit input-output industry level, the focal industry’s customer-industry R&D measure is the sum across customer industries (excluding the focal industry) of each customer industry’s annual R&D expense divided by total assets, weighted by the percentage of focal-industry output sold to that customer industry. The weights exclude exports and include personal consumption, private fixed investment, and government consumption/investment as final uses. Final-use R&D intensity is set to zero for personal consumption and to the mean customer-industry R&D intensity for private fixed investment and government consumption/investment. Industry R&D is aggregate Compustat R&D expense divided by aggregate industry assets; missing R&D values are set to zero. Where a six-digit IO industry has no Compustat firms, the authors use five-, four-, two-, then one-digit firms. IO weights use the 1987 Use table for 1984–1989, the 1992 table for 1990–1994, and annual updates of the 1992 benchmark tables for 1995–2003.
